messages.subject: 2 little Issues : 1.) Ignore NA's while counting 2.) X-Axis labeling
parts:
Hi @all,

I hope you can help me with that, it should not be that difficult, but
I was not able to find a solution in the book.

First Problem :

I want to compare the counts of 2 different sets (one is a subset of
the other) :

#For the Superset, every single row of the dataframe shall be counted
by ggplot, therefore I simply create a #character-variable, called
"All Groups"

dataframe$superset <- "All Groups"

#The subset-variable gets a certain subsetstring, where the subsetid's
correspond

dataframe$subset[dataframe$subsetid==value] <- dataframe$subsetstring
[dataframe$subsetid==value]

#Furthermore I got a factor to fill (cant come up with original data,
sorry) and the years, where I want to facet over

attach(dataframe)

ggplot(dataframe, aes(c(subset[is.na(subset)==FALSE], superset),
fill=afactor))+
geom_bar(position="fill")+
facet_grid(. ~ years, scales = "free_x", space = "free")+
scale_colour_gradientn(colour = rainbow(7))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(angle=90, hjust=1, size=15))

Now I get an error-message like this : "Different number of rows for
subset, superset." That is correct. How I can display it anyway ?

Second Problem :

I have gigantic x-Axis lables (for the Subset to be exact). How can I
display them like a sentence, that there is a line break after every
word ? It is something with opts, but how do I have to set the
parameters that it works ? Does anyone have an idea ?

Thanks in advance and have a nice day :-)

Kind Regards,

Ed

messages.subject: Re: 2 little Issues : 1.) Ignore NA's while counting 2.) X-Axis labeling
parts:
Hi Ed,

I'm having a hard time understanding the first problem (a small
reproducible example would help). Here's the second -

> Second Problem :
>
> I have gigantic x-Axis lables (for the Subset to be exact). How can I
> display them like a sentence, that there is a line break after every
> word ? It is something with opts, but how do I have to set the
> parameters that it works ? Does anyone have an idea ?

+ xlab('title')

If you need to break the title up by running over a line, in the text
but \n, as in

+ xlab('The quick brown fox jumps\nover the lazy dog.')

Hope it helps
david.

Hey again,

thanks for your help, David, but sorry I explained it completely wrong
with the X-Axis-Lables. I actually meant the representation of value-
names on the X-Axis :-D. Is there any way to display them with \n ?

For the second issue :

A little example :

library(ggplot2)

a <- data.frame(superset=1:8,subset=1:8,years=1:8,fillvariable=1:8)
a$superset <- c(1,1,1,1,1,1,2,3)
a$subset[a$superset==1] <- a$superset
a$subset[a$superset!=1] <- NA
a$years <- c(2000,2001,2000,2002,2000,2002,2003,2000)
a$fillvariable <- c("A","A","B","C","C","B","A","A")

attach(a)

ggplot(a, aes(c(superset,subset), fill=fillvariable))+

geom_bar(position="fill")+
facet_grid(. ~ years, scales = "free_x", space = "free")+
scale_colour_gradientn(colour = rainbow(7))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(angle=90, hjust=1, size=15))

Here the superset and subset shall be displayed side by side. But it
does not work, because they have different amounts of rows, which
should not be
a big deal, because I want to use "fill". But R spits out an error :-(

Best Regards,

Ed

Hi Ed,

> ggplot(a, aes(c(superset,subset), fill=fillvariable))+

This specification doesn't make sense - how do you expect fill to line
up with a variable that's not the same length? I don't understand
what you are trying to achieve with this plot, but maybe you need to
rbind together two data frames.
